shortcut_explanation: A square root is not half. √16 is 4, because 4 × 4 = 16.
full_explanation: √16 asks which number times itself makes 16. That number is 4. Half of 16 is 8. 8 is more than 4. So the answer is B: Quantity B is greater.

quantity_b: \text{the perimeter of a square with side } 5
shortcut_explanation: Go once around each shape. 7 + 3 + 7 + 3 = 20, and 5 + 5 + 5 + 5 = 20.
full_explanation: The perimeter is the distance all the way around. The rectangle has two sides of 7 and two sides of 3, which make 20. The square has four sides of 5, which also make 20. So the answer is C: the two quantities are equal.

shortcut_explanation: The middle number is 3, and there are 5 numbers. So the sum is 3 × 5 = 15.
full_explanation: Pair the outside numbers: 1 + 5 = 6 and 2 + 4 = 6. With the 3 in the middle, that makes 6 + 6 + 3 = 15. 15 is less than 16. So the answer is B: Quantity B is greater.

shortcut_explanation: 3/10 is three tenths, which is 0.3. 0.03 is only three hundredths.
full_explanation: The first place after the point is tenths, and the second place is hundredths. 3/10 is 0.3, with the 3 in the tenths place. 0.03 has its 3 in the hundredths place, so it is ten times smaller. So the answer is A: Quantity A is greater.

shortcut_explanation: 100% is the whole thing, so 200% is double. Double 10 is 20.
full_explanation: 100% of 10 is 10, the whole amount. 200% is two whole amounts: 10 + 10 = 20. 20 is more than 15. So the answer is A: Quantity A is greater.

quantity_a: \text{the number of odd numbers from } 1 \text{ to } 9
shortcut_explanation: List them: 1, 3, 5, 7, 9. That is 5 numbers.
full_explanation: Odd numbers are the ones you can't split into two equal whole-number halves. From 1 to 9 they are 1, 3, 5, 7 and 9. Counting them gives 5. So the answer is C: the two quantities are equal.

shortcut_explanation: A half plus a third is less than a half plus a half. So it is less than 1.
full_explanation: A third is smaller than a half. So a half plus a third is smaller than a half plus a half, which is 1. In sixths: 3/6 + 2/6 = 5/6. So the answer is B: Quantity B is greater.

quantity_a: \text{the angle that makes a straight line with a } 130 \text{ degree angle}
shortcut_explanation: Angles on a straight line add up to 180°. 180 − 130 = 50.
full_explanation: A straight line is a half turn, which is 180 degrees. The two angles share it, so the missing one is 180 − 130 = 50. 50 is less than 60. So the answer is B: Quantity B is greater.

shortcut_explanation: Do the inside first: (−3)² = 9. Then √9 = 3, never −3.
full_explanation: (−3)² = −3 × −3 = 9, because a negative times a negative is positive. √9 means the non-negative number that times itself makes 9, which is 3. 3 is more than −3. So the answer is A: Quantity A is greater.

shortcut_explanation: Line up the points: 1.01 − 0.10 = 0.91. 0.91 is a bit more than 0.90.
full_explanation: Write 0.1 as 0.10 so both numbers have two places after the point. 1.01 − 0.10 = 0.91. Compare 0.91 with 0.90: 91 hundredths beat 90 hundredths. So the answer is A: Quantity A is greater.

shortcut_explanation: 25% is a quarter. A quarter of 80 is 20, and 80 + 20 = 100.
full_explanation: A 25% rise adds a quarter of the starting amount. A quarter of 80 is 80 ÷ 4 = 20. 80 + 20 = 100. So the answer is C: the two quantities are equal.

shortcut_explanation: Test 0 as well. At x = 0 both sides are 0, but at x = 1, A is 1 and B is −1.
full_explanation: |x| is never negative, so −|x| is never positive. If x = 1, A is 1 and B is −1, so A wins. If x = 0, both are 0, a tie. Two different results mean you can't tell. So the answer is D: not enough information.

shortcut_explanation: An odd power keeps the sign. Try x = 1, then x = −1.
full_explanation: If x = 1, then x³ = 1, which is more than 0. If x = −1, then x³ = −1 × −1 × −1 = −1, which is less than 0. Three negatives multiplied make a negative. So the answer is D: not enough information.

quantity_a: \text{km travelled in } 15 \text{ minutes at } 60 \text{ km per hour}
shortcut_explanation: 60 km per hour is 1 km every minute. In 15 minutes that is 15 km.
full_explanation: An hour has 60 minutes, so 60 km per hour means 1 km each minute. 15 minutes then gives 15 km. 15 is less than 20. So the answer is B: Quantity B is greater.

shortcut_explanation: 6 lots of 17 plus 4 lots of 17 is 10 lots of 17. That is 170.
full_explanation: Both parts multiply 17. Put them together: 6 + 4 = 10 lots of 17. 17 × 10 = 170. So the answer is C: the two quantities are equal.

shortcut_explanation: (2³)² is 2³ × 2³, which is six 2s multiplied. 2⁶ beats 2⁵.
full_explanation: 2³ = 8, and 8² = 8 × 8 = 64. 2⁵ = 32. Squaring 2³ gives 2³ × 2³ = 2⁶, one more 2 than 2⁵. So the answer is A: Quantity A is greater.

quantity_a: \text{the longest whole-number length the third side can have}
shortcut_explanation: The third side must be shorter than 4 + 6 = 10. The biggest whole number below 10 is 9.
full_explanation: Two sides of a triangle together must be longer than the third side. So the third side is less than 4 + 6 = 10. A side of 9 still works, but a side of 10 would make the triangle lie flat. That makes 9 the longest. So the answer is C: the two quantities are equal.

shortcut_explanation: Try x = 2, then x = ½. Dividing 1 by a number less than 1 gives more than 1.
full_explanation: If x = 2, then 1/x = ½, which is less than 1. If x = ½, then 1/x = 2, because two halves fit in 1. That is more than 1. So the answer is D: not enough information.

condition: x \text{ and } 2x \text{ are angles that make a straight line}
shortcut_explanation: x and 2x make 180°, so 3x = 180 and x = 60.
full_explanation: Angles on a straight line add up to 180 degrees. x + 2x is three x's, so each x is 180 ÷ 3 = 60. 60 is less than 90. So the answer is B: Quantity B is greater.

shortcut_explanation: n is negative, so more lots of n go further below 0. 1000 × n is the more negative one.
full_explanation: Try n = −1: 999 × −1 = −999 and 1000 × −1 = −1000. −999 is closer to 0, so it is bigger. Each extra lot of a negative number pulls the total down. So the answer is A: Quantity A is greater.

shortcut_explanation: 0.5² = 0.25. Any x below 0.5 has a smaller square.
full_explanation: 0.5 × 0.5 = 0.25. When x is smaller than 0.5, x × x is smaller than 0.5 × 0.5. Try x = 0.3: 0.3² = 0.09, which is less than 0.25. So the answer is B: Quantity B is greater.

shortcut_explanation: 15 is 25% of 60. So it depends on whether x is above or below 25.
full_explanation: If x = 30, then 30% of 60 is 18, which is more than 15. If x = 20, then 20% of 60 is 12, which is less than 15. Both 20 and 30 are between 0 and 50. So the answer is D: not enough information.

quantity_b: \text{the average of } a, b \text{ and } c
condition: \text{a fourth number, equal to the average of } a, b \text{ and } c, \text{ is added to them}
shortcut_explanation: Adding a number equal to the average doesn't pull the average up or down.
full_explanation: Try 1, 2 and 6: their average is 3. Add a 3, and the four numbers 1, 2, 6 and 3 add up to 12. 12 ÷ 4 = 3, the same average as before. So the answer is C: the two quantities are equal.

shortcut_explanation: √x times √x is just x. And x is less than x + 1.
full_explanation: √x is the number that times itself makes x. So √x × √x = x. Try x = 9: 3 × 3 = 9, and 9 + 1 = 10. B is always 1 more. So the answer is B: Quantity B is greater.

shortcut_explanation: Undo both sides: y is 6 more than x.
full_explanation: x + 3 = y − 3. Add 3 to both sides: x + 6 = y. So y is always 6 more than x. Try x = 1: then y = 7. So the answer is B: Quantity B is greater.

shortcut_explanation: Multiply each part of the first bracket by each part of the second: x², 3x, 2x and 6.
full_explanation: x × x = x², x × 3 = 3x, 2 × x = 2x, and 2 × 3 = 6. 3x + 2x = 5x, so the total is x² + 5x + 6. Try x = 1: 3 × 4 = 12, and 1 + 5 + 6 = 12. So the answer is C: the two quantities are equal.

shortcut_explanation: The top is bigger than the bottom, so the fraction is more than 1.
full_explanation: With x positive, x + 1 is bigger than x. A fraction whose top is bigger than its bottom is more than 1. Try x = 4: 5/4 = 1¼. So the answer is A: Quantity A is greater.

quantity_b: \text{the remainder when } n \text{ is divided by } 10
condition: n \text{ is a whole number and } n > 10
shortcut_explanation: A remainder when you divide by 10 is at most 9. n is more than 10.
full_explanation: Dividing by 10 leaves a remainder from 0 to 9, the last digit of n. n is more than 10, so it beats any of those. Try n = 23: the remainder is 3. So the answer is A: Quantity A is greater.

shortcut_explanation: y = 18 is 3 parts, so each part is 6. x is 2 parts, which is 12, and 12 + 18 = 30.
full_explanation: The ratio splits things into parts of the same size. y is 3 parts and equals 18, so one part is 18 ÷ 3 = 6. x is 2 parts: 2 × 6 = 12. 12 + 18 = 30. So the answer is C: the two quantities are equal.

shortcut_explanation: Try a big x and a small x. x = 6 gives 2 and ½, but x = 1 gives ⅓ and 3.
full_explanation: If x = 6, then x/3 = 2 and 3/x = ½, so A wins. If x = 1, then x/3 = ⅓ and 3/x = 3, so B wins. Two different results mean you can't tell. So the answer is D: not enough information.

shortcut_explanation: x > 2y sounds like x is bigger, but test negatives. Try y = 1, then y = −2.
full_explanation: If x = 3 and y = 1, then 3 > 2, and x is more than y. If x = −3 and y = −2, then −3 > −4, but x is less than y. Doubling a negative number makes it smaller. So the answer is D: not enough information.

shortcut_explanation: x² − 6x + 9 is (x − 3)². Its square root is the distance between x and 3, and x is below 3.
full_explanation: (x − 3)² = x² − 6x + 9, so A is √((x − 3)²). A square root is never negative, so it is the distance from x to 3. With x below 3, that distance is 3 − x. Try x = 1: √4 = 2, and 3 − 1 = 2. So the answer is C: the two quantities are equal.

shortcut_explanation: For x between 0 and 1, x² is smaller than x. Dividing 1 by a smaller number gives a bigger answer.
full_explanation: Try x = ½: 1/x = 2, but x² = ¼, so 1/x² = 4. Squaring a fraction between 0 and 1 makes it smaller. A smaller bottom makes a bigger fraction. So the answer is B: Quantity B is greater.

shortcut_explanation: The fraction bar halves the whole top, so A is x/2 + 2, not x + 2. Try x = 0, then x = 2.
full_explanation: If x = 0, A is 4 ÷ 2 = 2 and B is 2, a tie. If x = 2, A is 6 ÷ 2 = 3 and B is 4, so B wins. Halving x + 4 halves the x as well as the 4. So the answer is D: not enough information.

quantity_a: \text{the percent increase from } a \text{ to } b
quantity_b: \text{the percent decrease from } b \text{ to } a
shortcut_explanation: Both changes are the same amount, b − a. The same change is a bigger percent of the smaller number a.
full_explanation: Try a = 50 and b = 100. Going up by 50 from 50 is a 100% increase. Going down by 50 from 100 is only a 50% decrease. The same change is a bigger share of the smaller number. So the answer is A: Quantity A is greater.

shortcut_explanation: For positive powers 3 wins, but negative powers flip. Try x = 1, then x = −1.
full_explanation: If x = 1, 3¹ = 3 beats 2¹ = 2. If x = −1, 3⁻¹ = ⅓ and 2⁻¹ = ½, and ½ is bigger. A negative power means 1 divided by the positive power. So the answer is D: not enough information.

shortcut_explanation: Dividing by a negative number flips the order. a is bigger, so a/c is smaller.
full_explanation: Try a = 6, b = 2 and c = −2. Then a/c = −3 and b/c = −1, and −1 is bigger. Dividing by a negative turns big positives into big negatives. So the answer is B: Quantity B is greater.

condition: n \text{ is a whole number from } 1 \text{ to } 15
shortcut_explanation: Dividing by 9 leaves the same remainder as the digit sum does. 10ⁿ is a 1 and some 0s, so its digits add up to 1.
full_explanation: 10 = 9 + 1, 100 = 99 + 1, and 1000 = 999 + 1. Numbers like 9, 99 and 999 divide by 9 exactly. That makes every 10ⁿ a multiple of 9 plus 1, so the remainder is 1. So the answer is C: the two quantities are equal.

shortcut_explanation: a is 3 parts and b is 4 parts, so a + b is 7 parts. 7 parts divided by 4 parts is 7/4, which is less than 2.
full_explanation: Count in parts: a + b is 3 + 4 = 7 parts, and b is 4 parts. So the fraction is 7/4 = 1¾. 2 would need a + b to be 8 parts. So the answer is B: Quantity B is greater.

shortcut_explanation: xy < 0 means one number is positive and one is negative. Adding them cancels some, but A adds both distances.
full_explanation: Try x = 5 and y = −2: A is 5 + 2 = 7, but B is |3| = 3. When the signs are different, adding x and y takes part of one away. A never loses anything. So the answer is A: Quantity A is greater.

shortcut_explanation: Turn both into tenth powers: 3²⁰ = 9¹⁰ and 2³⁰ = 8¹⁰. 9 beats 8.
full_explanation: 3²⁰ is (3²)¹⁰ = 9¹⁰, because twenty 3s make ten groups of two 3s. 2³⁰ is (2³)¹⁰ = 8¹⁰. Both are ten copies multiplied, and 9 is bigger than 8. So the answer is A: Quantity A is greater.

shortcut_explanation: For positive x, A is more than 1 and B is less than 1. Then test a negative, like x = −3.
full_explanation: If x = 1, A is 2 and B is ½, so A wins. If x = −3, A is −2/−3 = ⅔ and B is −3/−2 = 1½, so B wins. A negative x can flip the sizes. So the answer is D: not enough information.

quantity_a: \text{each angle of a shape with } n \text{ equal sides and } n \text{ equal angles}
condition: n \text{ is a whole number and } n > 4
shortcut_explanation: A square has four 90° corners. With more equal sides, each corner opens wider.
full_explanation: Walk around the shape: you make one full turn of 360 degrees in n equal turns. Each turn is 360 ÷ n, which is less than 90 when n is more than 4. Each inside angle is 180 minus that turn, so it is more than 90. So the answer is A: Quantity A is greater.

quantity_a: \text{the average speed for the whole trip, in km per hour}
condition: \text{a car drives } 120 \text{ km at } 40 \text{ km per hour, then } 120 \text{ km back at } 60 \text{ km per hour}
shortcut_explanation: The car spends more time at the slower speed. So the average is below the halfway speed of 50.
full_explanation: Going takes 120 ÷ 40 = 3 hours, and coming back takes 120 ÷ 60 = 2 hours. That is 240 km in 5 hours, which is 48 km per hour. 48 is less than 50. So the answer is B: Quantity B is greater.

quantity_a: \text{the price after a } 25\% \text{ rise and then a } 20\% \text{ fall}
shortcut_explanation: A 25% rise multiplies by 5/4. A 20% fall multiplies by 4/5. 5/4 × 4/5 = 1.
full_explanation: Try p = 100. A 25% rise gives 125. 20% of 125 is 25, so the fall takes it back to 100. The fall is a smaller percent, but of a bigger number. So the answer is C: the two quantities are equal.

shortcut_explanation: 1/3 as a decimal is 0.3333…, with 3s that never stop. 0.333 stops after three of them.
full_explanation: 1 ÷ 3 = 0.3333…, and the 3s go on forever. 0.333 is a little short of that, by about 3 ten-thousandths. Close is not the same as equal. So the answer is A: Quantity A is greater.

quantity_a: \text{the sum of the odd numbers from } 1 \text{ to } 19
shortcut_explanation: Adding the first n odd numbers always makes n². From 1 to 19 there are 10 odd numbers.
full_explanation: Pair them from the outside: 1 + 19, 3 + 17, 5 + 15, 7 + 13 and 9 + 11. That is 5 pairs of 20, which is 100. And 10² = 100 too. So the answer is C: the two quantities are equal.

condition: x \text{ is a whole number from } 1 \text{ to } 10
shortcut_explanation: −2ˣ means −(2ˣ), always negative. (−2)ˣ is negative for odd x and positive for even x.
full_explanation: If x = 3: −2³ = −8 and (−2)³ = −8, a tie. If x = 2: −2² = −4, but (−2)² = 4, so B wins. Do the power before the minus sign unless there are brackets. So the answer is D: not enough information.

shortcut_explanation: Test 0. If x = 0 and y = −1, both sides are 0. But x = 2 and y = 1 gives 4 and 2.
full_explanation: If x = 2 and y = 1, A is 4 × 1 = 4 and B is 2 × 1 = 2, so A wins. If x = 0 and y = −1, both sides are 0, a tie. Two different results mean you can't tell. So the answer is D: not enough information.

shortcut_explanation: An odd power keeps the order and the sign. If x³ is smaller, x is smaller.
full_explanation: Cubing never swaps two numbers: a bigger number always has a bigger cube, even for negatives. Try x = −2 and y = 1: −8 < 1, and −2 < 1. Squares are different, because they hide the sign. So the answer is B: Quantity B is greater.
